novelty.justification: The claim’s core new-mechanism hypothesis is that a “shared, language-agnostic representation of the SOURCE” is bound late to evidential morphology and that “the same source variable causally governs the model’s EXPRESSED CERTAINTY,” with cross-language misbinding explaining both marking and calibration errors. Searches using “multilingual LLM evidentiality hidden representations,” “information source activation steering confidence,” “Turkish evidential morphology LLM,” and “cross-lingual latent grammatical concepts” identify the closest work as Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish (2026), which behaviorally studies source trust and Turkish markers, and How do LLMs Compute Verbal Confidence (2026), which mechanistically studies confidence representations but not evidential source or multilingual grammatical binding. Moving from those separate lines to a single causal latent variable jointly controlling language-specific evidential realization and certainty requires a new core relationship rather than a direct transfer, although the shared-representation and late-binding components are natural extensions of multilingual concept-probing work and the probing/patching/steering tools are standard.
